pages.reference: Read this value as held by a Christian traditionalist in the United States, with the religious right as the cultural reference. Tradition here concerns preserving, observing or passing down identifiable inherited customs, religious practices and ways of life, valued for their continuity with the past. Religious endorsement of a general moral goal alone does not establish that connection.
pages.description: H.R.5408 would require an employer to begin bargaining soon after its workers vote to form a union. If the two sides cannot agree on a first contract, the dispute may proceed to federal mediation and, if mediation fails, to an arbitration panel whose decision would be binding.
pages.comparison: If this bill took effect on June 9, 2026, versus law in force then

directions.heading: Does this value give [NAME] a reason to favor H.R.5408?
directions.main_effect_html: Main effect The bill gives newly unionized workers a way to reach a first contract both sides must follow. Under the law in force on June 9, 2026, employers must bargain, but the law “does not impose any deadline or mandate that the parties achieve a collective bargaining agreement.” [1] After bargaining and mediation (help from a third party to reach agreement) fail, the bill requires a panel to settle the dispute: “A majority of the 3-person arbitration panel shall render a decision settling the dispute and such decision shall be binding upon the parties for a period of 2 years, unless amended during such period by written consent of the parties.” [2] It also requires employers “to maintain current wages, hours, and terms and conditions of employment pending an agreement” [2].

points.title: Counting family needs in pay decisions supports the traditional single-income family arrangement.
points.pro_html:
Point 1 Counting family needs in pay decisions supports the traditional single-income family arrangement.

  • Because The panel must base its decision partly on family support: “the employees' ability to sustain themselves, their families, and their dependents on the wages and benefits they earn from the employer” [2].
  • Because Southern Baptist teaching assigns a husband the duty to provide: “He has the God-given responsibility to provide for, to protect, and to lead his family.” [3]
  • Because Christian commentator Chuck Colson urged support for a family wage that “allows one parent to support a family on just one income.” [4]
  • Because The same Southern Baptist statement defines the marriage commitment these earnings support: “Marriage is the uniting of one man and one woman in covenant commitment for a lifetime.” [3]
  • So The bill gives workers a legal claim to have the costs of supporting a family counted in binding pay decisions. That backs the means to sustain marriage and the roles of a father providing and a mother caring for children at home—customs [NAME] values preserving.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: The bill’s family-support factor is one of five, with no stated priority and no single-income standard. The family-wage standard in the Colson commentary is pay that allows one parent to support a family on one income. Sources: [2], [4].

points.title: Protecting work schedules helps families keep religious customs and pass on their faith.
points.pro_html:
Point 2 Protecting work schedules helps families keep religious customs and pass on their faith.

  • Because Keeping current terms until agreement protects existing schedules past a bargaining deadlock. Legal analysis identifies the change: “The FLCA’s second major change to the law of collective bargaining is the removal of the employer’s right to unilaterally implement its last, best, and final offer when the parties reach a good faith impasse.” [5]
  • Because Existing contracts protect time for worship. Kroger’s 2021–25 agreement gives specified groups of longtime workers this rule: “Sunday and holiday work shall be voluntary and rotated among qualified employees who are available for such work.” [6]
  • So The bill protects such established Sunday and holiday arrangements against changes an employer would otherwise impose after a deadlock.
  • Because First contracts also secure religious scheduling rules. Penn graduate workers announced: “Graduate Workers’ Agreement with the Penn administration has been ratified and it is now our first union contract.” [7] Their agreement states: “Graduate Workers may request reasonable schedule adjustments, including switching workdays, to observe religious holidays or cultural observances not recognized by the University. Such requests shall not be unreasonably denied.” [8]
  • Because Contracts also protect the notice families need to plan regular activities. Bloomingdale’s flagship-store union workers “receive their schedules twenty-one days in advance and must be notified of any changes to the schedule at least one week in advance.” [9]
  • Because Sunday worship is an established Christian custom. Southern Baptist teaching says the Lord’s Day “should include exercises of worship and spiritual devotion, both public and private.” [3]
  • Because Passing on faith needs regular family time. Focus on the Family explains: “For children to absorb God’s truths, regular times of family Bible study, devotion and worship are important.” [10]
  • So Preserving existing schedules protects worship routines. A binding route to first contracts strengthens workers’ means to obtain religious holiday and advance-notice rules. Both serve [NAME]’s commitment to keeping Christian customs and teaching them to children.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: Under Groff v. DeJoy (2023), an employer denying a religious accommodation under existing federal law must show substantial increased costs in relation to the conduct of its particular business. The cited schedule clauses come from negotiated contracts. Sources: [11].

points.title: Paid parental leave can help parents follow their religious rule against abortion.
points.pro_html:
Point 3 Paid parental leave can help parents follow their religious rule against abortion.

  • Because Paid parental leave is a concrete first-contract benefit. Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago workers’ first agreement includes: “Four weeks of paid parental leave upon the birth or adoption of a child” [12].
  • Because Lack of leave is a reported reason for seeking abortion in the United States. A mother interviewed in a U.S. study explained: “My work doesn't offer maternity leave” [13]. She added: “If I took time off I would lose my job so there's just no way.” [13]
  • Because Southern Baptist teaching makes protecting unborn life a religious duty: “We should speak on behalf of the unborn and contend for the sanctity of all human life from conception to natural death.” [3]
  • Because Christian pro-life writers John Stonestreet and Roberto Rivera apply that duty to supporting parents through leave policies: “We should also back policies that will encourage women to choose life.” [14]
  • So Binding first-contract settlement strengthens workers’ route to paid parental leave. For parents who observe the religious rule against abortion, that eases the work and income pressure described by the mother and helps them continue that observance.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: The museum’s first contract was ratified by members. In one Quebec first-contract award, an arbitrator declined to unbundle health and dental plans in a way that favored the union plan and found for the employer. Sources: [12], [15].

points.title: Making workers’ chosen unions effective helps carry out inherited Christian duties of fair treatment.
points.pro_html:
Point 4 Making workers’ chosen unions effective helps carry out inherited Christian duties of fair treatment.

  • Because Congress identifies a way delay weakens workers’ chosen unions: “The employers can use those delays to sap labor organization resolve and secure more favorable terms for the employer.” [2]
  • Because Adequate pay is a biblical duty: “God intends that people should be adequately paid for the work they do and enjoy food, shelter and clothing as part of the fruit of that work” [16].
  • Because In 1891, Pope Leo XIII described an employer’s duty: “His great and principal duty is to give every one what is just.” [17]
  • Because That teaching also called for worker associations to become “more numerous and more efficient.” [17]
  • So A binding route past stalled talks makes workers’ associations more able to press for adequate pay. Requiring family needs to count in the settlement gives that effort a concrete basis. This helps [NAME] carry Christian traditions of mutual help and fair treatment into working life.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: The panel has one union-selected, one employer-selected and one mutually agreed neutral member, and family needs are one of five factors. A close-election study reports wage estimates close to zero for new unionization from 1984 to 2001, without estimating first-contract arbitration. Sources: [2], [18].
points.retirement_reason: Fair pay and a religious endorsement of labor justice do not establish a particular tradition affected by this bill.

points.title: Mediation backed by a binding settlement supports Christian peacemaking at work.
points.pro_html:
Point 5 Mediation backed by a binding settlement supports Christian peacemaking at work.

  • Because When mediation is requested, the bill requires the federal mediation service to “use its best efforts, by mediation and conciliation, to secure an agreement.” [2]
  • Because First-contract arbitration (FCA) means a third party settles terms when bargaining fails. Studying this process in Canada, Susan Johnson reports: “I find that FCA reduces first agreement work stoppage incidence by at least 50 percent.” [19]
  • Because The study identifies an incentive shared by the bill’s binding-settlement process: “Together these results suggest that FCA encourages collective bargaining by creating an incentive for the parties to bargain in good faith and negotiate an agreement.” [19]
  • Because Southern Baptist teaching states: “It is the duty of Christians to seek peace with all men on principles of righteousness.” [3]
  • So The bill adds a binding way out of first-contract deadlocks and an incentive to settle before reaching that stage. This gives [NAME] a practical way to follow the Christian duty to seek peace in workplace disputes.
points.con_html:
Response The Canadian study does not separate the bill’s proposed incentive to settle from Canadian rules that restrict work stoppages.

  • Because Johnson’s Canadian cases include a rule absent from H.R.5408: “once an application for FCA is filed any work stoppage in progress must stop” [19]. First-contract arbitration, or FCA, means a third party sets the terms when bargaining fails.
  • Because The study combines different forms of arbitration: “There is not enough variation across Canadian jurisdictions in the use of different types of FCA to permit the analysis to estimate the affect of each type of FCA on incidence.” [19] Here, incidence means how often newly certified bargaining units have a first-contract strike or lockout.
  • So The reported reduction concerns Canadian systems that bundle arbitration with different rules on strikes and lockouts. It does not isolate what H.R.5408’s design would do. The proposed incentive to bargain is an explanation of that pattern, not a separately tested effect of the mechanism shared with this bill.
  • Because The religious standard is “to seek peace with all men on principles of righteousness” [3]. A strike or lockout count does not measure whether the parties treat each other justly or whether their settlement does so.
  • So The PRO has not connected this bill to fewer stoppages under its own rules or connected the study’s count to the just peace its religious source calls for. This response does not answer the narrower point that mediation and a binding settlement offer a way out of deadlock.
points.retirement_reason: Avoiding strikes serves peace and cooperation; religious praise of peace does not establish a particular inherited practice.

directions.heading: Does this value give [NAME] a reason to oppose H.R.5408?
directions.main_effect_html:
Main effect The bill requires a binding first contract when talks and mediation fail. After 90 days of bargaining, either side may request mediation. After 30 days from that request, subject to agreed extensions, the dispute goes to a panel: “A majority of the 3-person arbitration panel shall render a decision settling the dispute and such decision shall be binding upon the parties for a period of 2 years, unless amended during such period by written consent of the parties.” [2] Current law “does not impose any deadline or mandate that the parties achieve a collective bargaining agreement.” [1]

  • Because First-contract delays weaken new unions: “delay frustrates workers and undermines their union.” [20]
  • Because The Service Employees International Union (SEIU) exempts local unions from an added national payment for members without a first contract: “The additional per capita tax for the Unity Fund shall also not be payable on dues from members who have not achieved a first collective bargaining agreement.” [21]
  • Because Members' payments also support national political work. SEIU requires local payments “per member per month on all dues received by the Local Union.” [21] It assigns part to “political education and political action purposes” [21]. The American Federation of Teachers (AFT) states that “$2.90 of each member’s per capita tax shall be set aside each month in a special fund” [22] supporting “political activities” [22].
  • Because These unions organize private-sector workers. SEIU's constitution includes “working people in the public and private sector” [21]. AFT reports representing “more than 75,000 educators in charter schools who are considered private sector employees.” [23] It describes employers “wearing down a new union by refusing to negotiate a first contract.” [23]
  • So Securing first contracts removes a barrier to SEIU's national income and protects new unions against weakening through delay. That gives these organizations a firmer base for the positions and efforts below.
  • Note Protection for objecting nonmembers leaves the path through members' payments intact: “Section 8(a)(3) does not permit a union, over the objections of dues-paying nonmember employees, to expend funds collected from them on activities unrelated to collective-bargaining activities.” [24]

points.title: It strengthens organized opposition to the Christian tradition of protecting unborn life.
points.pro_html:
Point 1 It strengthens organized opposition to the Christian tradition of protecting unborn life.

  • Because The Southern Baptist Convention teaches: “Human life is sacred at every stage—from conception to natural death—because all people bear the image of God” [25].
  • Because This tradition calls for public action, not just private belief: “we urge all Southern Baptists to advocate in the public square for laws and policies that reflect the moral order revealed in Scripture and nature” [25].
  • Because SEIU pledges to “do everything in our power to keep abortion and all reproductive healthcare services safe, legal, and accessible for everyone” [26].
  • So A firmer income and membership base strengthens an organization working against a teaching [NAME]'s tradition calls on Christians to uphold in law. Preserving that teaching gives [NAME] a reason to oppose this effect.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: SEIU’s Unity Fund has a stated aim of winning pay, benefits and security; its political set-aside is decided annually by its board. AFT’s fund operates under council guidelines. The AFT letter says most of its members work in the public sector, which the bill does not cover. SEIU, AFT and federation sources state positions and funding rules but no measured effect of first contracts on political spending. Sources: [21], [22], [23].

points.title: It strengthens a federation that backs legal recognition of same-sex marriage against this tradition's teaching.
points.pro_html:
Point 2 It strengthens a federation that backs legal recognition of same-sex marriage against this tradition's teaching.

  • Because The Southern Baptist Convention teaches: “Marriage is a lifelong covenant between one man and one woman” [25]. It calls for “the overturning of laws and court rulings, including Obergefell v. Hodges, that defy God’s design for marriage and family” [25].
  • Because The AFL-CIO, a group of unions, lobbied for the opposite policy: “The AFL-CIO urges you to vote in support of HR 8404, the Respect for Marriage Act. This legislation is essential to securing marriage equality for same-gender couples” [27].
  • Because Paying members support the federation as well as their own unions. Its constitution requires payment “upon the full paid-up membership of each affiliated national or international union” [28]. AFT confirms: “The AFT is affiliated with American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations” [22].
  • So Protecting paying membership in affiliated unions supports a federation that lobbied in 2022 for a marriage policy this Christian tradition seeks to change. Absent a changed position, strengthening that federation conflicts with [NAME]'s aim of upholding its inherited view of marriage.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: The AFL-CIO letter is dated November 21, 2022, and the Respect for Marriage Act was signed on December 13, 2022; the packet has no later AFL-CIO marriage-policy source. AFT’s resolution pledging to work to reverse listed decisions, including Fulton, is dated July 17, 2022. AFT’s site notes generally that a newer resolution may have superseded an earlier one and that resolutions other than those from its most recent convention do not necessarily reflect current policy; the packet shows no superseding resolution, and it does not establish AFT’s current policy on Fulton. Sources: [27], [29], [30].

points.title: It strengthens campaigns to replace inherited Christian rules about sex with rules based on gender identity.
points.pro_html:
Point 3 It strengthens campaigns to replace inherited Christian rules about sex with rules based on gender identity.

  • Because The Southern Baptist Convention teaches: “God made every person in his image as either male or female in accord with his good design for humanity” [25]. It calls for laws that “recognize the biological reality of male and female” [25].
  • Because AFT's May 2025 policy seeks “strong state and national protections for LGBTQIA+ youth and adults” [31], including “Equitable access to facilities that match gender identities” [31] and “Policies that allow transgender athletes to compete in the sports teams that they identify with” [31].
  • So Strengthening AFT's member-funded political work supports concrete efforts to change public rules away from the understanding of sex [NAME] seeks to preserve.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: SEIU’s Unity Fund has a stated aim of winning pay, benefits and security; its political set-aside is decided annually by its board. AFT’s fund operates under council guidelines. The AFT letter says most of its members work in the public sector, which the bill does not cover. SEIU, AFT and federation sources state positions and funding rules but no measured effect of first contracts on political spending. Sources: [21], [22], [23].

points.title: It strengthens opposition to aid that helps families pass on their faith through Christian schools.
points.pro_html:
Point 4 It strengthens opposition to aid that helps families pass on their faith through Christian schools.

  • Because The Southern Baptist Convention says God “entrusted parents with the primary responsibility of raising, educating, and discipling their children” [25].
  • Because School aid helps families carry out that role. The Association of Christian Schools International reports: “School choice programs in Kansas, along with scholarships CCS itself provides, enable the school to welcome students who were previously unable to afford tuition” [32].
  • Because The report connects access to religious practice: “Because of school choice, some students are shepherded by Christian educators for the first time, which has made a positive impact in the home.” [32]
  • Because AFT pledges to “assist our affiliates in lobbying state governments, and will support affiliated unions in opposing school vouchers and voucher-like programs” [33]. These are forms of aid for schooling outside the public system.
  • So Stronger AFT resources support an opponent of aid that makes Christian schooling affordable. Preserving families' ability to teach and practice their faith gives [NAME] a reason to oppose that effect.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: SEIU’s Unity Fund has a stated aim of winning pay, benefits and security; its political set-aside is decided annually by its board. AFT’s fund operates under council guidelines. The AFT letter says most of its members work in the public sector, which the bill does not cover. SEIU, AFT and federation sources state positions and funding rules but no measured effect of first contracts on political spending. Sources: [21], [22], [23].

points.title: It strengthens opposition to military aid supported by the religious right's tradition of standing with Israel.
points.pro_html:
Point 5 It strengthens opposition to military aid supported by the religious right's tradition of standing with Israel.

  • Because Christians United for Israel grounds that tradition in Scripture. Its Action Fund chairwoman says: “If you don’t believe Christians should stand with Israel, you don’t believe the Bible” [34].
  • Because The group campaigns for security aid. Its founder praises “Advancing this security assistance” [35] to ensure “Israel has the vital support she needs to defeat our common enemies” [35].
  • Because SEIU joined unions calling on the president to “immediately halt all military aid to Israel” [36]. Its Committee of Interns and Residents reaffirmed this campaign in October 2025, citing a resolution that demanded “the end to military aid to Israel” [37] and reporting that members “have continued to organize inside and outside of CIR in solidarity with Palestine” [37].
  • So A firmer base for SEIU strengthens an organized opponent of a concrete way this religious tradition acts on its biblical commitments. Honoring that practice gives [NAME] a reason to oppose that effect.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: SEIU’s Unity Fund has a stated aim of winning pay, benefits and security; its political set-aside is decided annually by its board. AFT’s fund operates under council guidelines. The AFT letter says most of its members work in the public sector, which the bill does not cover. SEIU, AFT and federation sources state positions and funding rules but no measured effect of first contracts on political spending. Sources: [21], [22], [23].
points.retirement_reason: A contemporary coalition's position on military aid to Israel is not itself an inherited practice; the argument does not establish a further effect on religious observance or transmission.

points.title: It strengthens a stated pledge to remove legal protection for carrying Christian teaching into charitable work.
points.pro_html:
Point 6 It strengthens a stated pledge to remove legal protection for carrying Christian teaching into charitable work.

  • Because The Supreme Court described Catholic Social Services' foster care as “continuing the centuries-old mission of the Catholic Church to serve Philadelphia’s needy children.” [38]
  • Because The court's account states: “CSS holds the religious belief that marriage is a sacred bond between a man and a woman.” [38] The Southern Baptist Convention's Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission explains that the ruling lets faith-based providers “continue serving children and families according to their convictions.” [39]
  • Because AFT's 2022 resolution lists “Fulton v. City of Philadelphia (2021)” [30] among the rulings it condemns, then pledges to “work to reverse both these decisions of the court and their impact” [30].
  • So To the extent AFT maintains that pledge, strengthening it supports opposition to protection for practicing inherited Christian beliefs while serving others. [NAME]'s concern for following religious customs reaches this freedom to act on faith, as well as the beliefs themselves.
points.notes_html: Evidence note: The AFL-CIO letter is dated November 21, 2022, and the Respect for Marriage Act was signed on December 13, 2022; the packet has no later AFL-CIO marriage-policy source. AFT’s resolution pledging to work to reverse listed decisions, including Fulton, is dated July 17, 2022. AFT’s site notes generally that a newer resolution may have superseded an earlier one and that resolutions other than those from its most recent convention do not necessarily reflect current policy; the packet shows no superseding resolution, and it does not establish AFT’s current policy on Fulton. Sources: [27], [29], [30].

points.title: For contracts set by a panel, it removes a vote workers can use to reject health coverage that conflicts with their faith.
points.pro_html:
Point 7 For contracts set by a panel, it removes a vote workers can use to reject health coverage that conflicts with their faith.

  • Because Contract approval is an existing union practice: “nearly all union constitutions and bylaws require union members’ ratification of collective bargaining agreements before they are signed and enforced.” [1] Ratification means a vote to approve the contract.
  • Because AFT seeks “transgender-inclusive healthcare” [40] “during bargaining negotiations with employers” [40]. Its 2025 policy also calls for “gender-affirming medical care” [31] to “be fully covered by medical insurance” [31].
  • Because Choosing coverage is itself a religious practice in this tradition. GuideStone, a Southern Baptist body, warns: “you could be required to pay premiums that go toward other members’ coverage that directly conflicts with your faith — even when you don’t personally use a medical product or service that goes against your convictions.” [41] It explains its own approach: “GuideStone health plans exclude coverage for gender dysphoria treatments, including sex change surgery or related sex hormones.” [41]
  • Because For a contract set by the panel, its decision “shall be binding upon the parties for a period of 2 years” [2]. Members' approval is no longer a condition for those terms to take effect.
  • So Even where a majority would reject such coverage to follow their faith, a panel can make it part of their contract. The bill removes their collective vote as a way to keep shared health coverage in line with inherited Christian teaching.
points.notes_html:
Evidence note: AFT’s bargaining resolution on transgender-inclusive health care dates from 2017. AFT’s site notes that older resolutions may not reflect current policy; its 2025 resolution separately supports coverage. Sources: [40], [31].

Evidence note: After an overall impasse, employers generally may impose a final offer, and a union can break the impasse by showing that resumed bargaining might be fruitful, which suspends the employer’s reliance on that offer. The bill requires current terms to continue pending an agreement. A CRS primer says prospective federal action is generally subject to RFRA; whether RFRA applies to an award by this panel is unresolved in the packet. A 2017 AFT resolution commits it to promote healthcare policies that expressly cover transgender employees’ needs; it does not show what a panel would award. Sources: [42], [43], [40], [2].
